record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: For an Archimedean atomic effect algebra E with atomic center C(E), find conditions equivalent to the effect-algebraic sum of all atoms of C(E), computed in E, being equal to 1. Also find conditions equivalent to the equality between the sum of an arbitrary subset D of C(E) computed in E and the corresponding sum computed in C(E), whenever at least one of these sums exists.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. An effect algebra is a structure $(E, \oplus, 0, 1)$ where $\oplus$ is a partial binary operation on $E$ satisfying: (E1) commutativity — if $a\oplus b$ is defined then $b\oplus a$ is defined and $a\oplus b = b\oplus a$; (E2) associativity — if $a\oplus b$ and $(a\oplus b)\oplus c$ are defined then $b\oplus c$ and $a\oplus(b\oplus c)$ are defined and equal; (E3) for every $a\in E$ there is a unique $a'\in E$ with $a\oplus a' = 1$; (E4) if $a\oplus 1$ is defined, then $a = 0$. A partial order is defined by $a\le b$ iff there exists $c\in E$ with $a\oplus c = b$.

An element $a\in E$ is an atom if $0<a$ and $0<x\le a$ implies $x=a$. The effect algebra $E$ is atomic if for every nonzero $b\in E$ there is an atom $a\le b$, and is Archimedean if for every atom $a$ the iterated sum $na = a\oplus a\oplus\cdots\oplus a$ ($n$ times) fails to exist for some finite $n$.

An element $z\in E$ is central if $E$ decomposes as $E\cong [0,z]\times [0,z']$ via the natural map. The set $C(E)$ of central elements is a sub-effect-algebra of $E$, called the center.

For an arbitrary indexed family $\{a_i\}_{i\in I}\subseteq E$, the effect-algebraic sum $\bigoplus_{i\in I} a_i$, when it exists, is the supremum of the finite partial sums (formed by $\oplus$).

Problem. Let $E$ be an Archimedean atomic effect algebra and let $C(E)$ be its center, which is itself atomic. 

(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on $E$ for the effect-algebraic sum $\bigoplus\{c : c\text{ is an atom of }C(E)\}$, computed in $E$, to exist and to equal $1$.

(b) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on $E$ for the following property to hold: for every subset $D\subseteq C(E)$ such that at least one of the sums $\bigoplus_{d\in D} d$ computed in $E$ or $\bigoplus_{d\in D} d$ computed in $C(E)$ exists, both sums exist and are equal.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns characterizations related to atomic centers of Archimedean atomic effect algebras. Related works (Paseka–Riečanová and others, around 2010) give sufficient conditions, e.g., when the supremum of all central atoms equals 1 the effect algebra decomposes as a direct product of irreducibles; it was also shown that C(E) need not be a bifull sublattice. However, no source directly stating that the full equivalent-conditions characterization asked here has been completely settled was located, so the status is taken as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Archimedean Atomic Lattice Effect Algebras with Complete Lattice of Sharp Elements
status_evidence.snippet: Studies central atoms and decompositions of Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Provides sufficient conditions related to sums of central atoms but not the full equivalences requested.

status_evidence.title: On central atoms of Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates properties of central atoms in Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results exist but the problem's full characterization status is not confirmed.

status_evidence.title: An atomic MV-effect algebra with non-atomic center
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs an atomic effect algebra whose center is not atomic.
status_evidence.claim: Shows subtleties that motivate the problem of comparing sums in E and in C(E).
